papers.title: Learn Your Own Thoughts: Abstract Token Curriculum

summary.tldr: Abstract Token Curriculum (ATC) is a novel curriculum learning framework that trains LLMs to generate continuous, unsupervised intermediate CoT representations by gradually increasing problem complexity.
key_points: Eliminates the need for explicit token supervision or manual scratchpad design in CoT reasoning.
Trains models across a sequence of increasingly complex distributions to form internal abstract representations in continuous space.
Theoretical proofs demonstrate that for single-layer softmax attention learning parity functions, ATC focuses attention on CoT context tokens offering the easiest next-token prediction path.
Empirically validated on graph reachability and arithmetic learning tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: ATC enables language models to develop internal reasoning capabilities without relying on expensive, task-specific CoT datasets or hand-engineered intermediate steps.

papers.title: Chronicle: Cut-Point Replay for Regression Testing of LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Chronicle introduces cut-point replay for LLM agents, recording non-deterministic boundaries into immutable envelopes to execute mixed live-and-recorded regression tests in continuous integration.
key_points: Records agent runs at non-deterministic boundaries with an overhead of 23 μs per crossing (0.008% of a 300 ms model call).
Cut-point replay serves a subset of boundaries from the immutable record while executing new code live for the complementary subset.
Full replay makes no model calls and achieves bit-stability across 20 repetitions.
In a mutation study, cut-point tests caught 100% of mutants that permitted recorded unsafe actions, whereas stubbing all boundaries caught 0%.
Evaluated on a benchmark of 6 recorded failures; code and benchmark are open-sourced on GitHub.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deterministic, low-overhead regression testing of LLM agent failures within CI/CD pipelines without making live model calls for unchanged boundaries.

papers.title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness

summary.tldr: SoL-Pi scales auto-research loops at the agent harness layer to optimize long-trajectory recursive self-improvement while dramatically reducing token consumption.
key_points: Applies recursive self-improvement (RSI) principles to the harness layer across diverse environments.
Implements four core mechanisms: action execution, context compaction, observation handling, and delegated reading.
Achieves performance comparable to Pi on the 51-task EdgeBench using GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5.
Reduces recorded token traffic by 44.7-49.0% and lowers API costs by approximately one third.
Generates estimated hourly cost savings of $8.75-$13.50 compared to native Codex and Claude Code harnesses.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that automated harness optimization can maintain agent benchmark performance while cutting API token usage and costs nearly in half for unattended execution.

papers.title: How Do Agent Harnesses Create Value? Planning Information and Release Control in Stateful LLM Agents

summary.tldr: An empirical study shows task-specific planning harnesses boost LLM agent success by 7.17 percentage points, while read-only terminal verifiers cost under $0.01 per episode and block 61% of invalid task completions.
key_points: In a 265-cell experiment on tau^2-bench, prewritten task-specific plans (Fixed) improved oracle-verified success by 7.17 percentage points over word-count-matched shuffled policies (Sham).
Planning gains were concentrated in higher-complexity tasks across two Retail experiments and an Airline pilot.
A read-only terminal verifier rejected 61% of oracle-invalid Retail episodes while withholding 17% of valid ones, costing less than $0.01 extra per episode.
Under high-liability scenarios where false acceptances carry heavy loss, standalone terminal verifiers capture almost all false-pass prevention benefits at a fraction of full-stack costs.
summary.why_it_matters: Determining whether to deploy planning guidance or verification depends on deployment liability, with low-cost terminal verifiers providing the primary value in high-liability environments.

papers.title: SkillAA: Attribution-Guided Skill-Graph Updating with Targeted Validation and Rollback

summary.tldr: SkillAA introduces a framework that uses abductive attribution to route failure fixes to specific nodes within a unified skill graph, validating edits via Local and Big Gates for frozen LLMs.
key_points: SkillAA unifies skill applicability, execution, and topological dependencies into a single graph used for selection, localized repair, and validation.
Attribution routes updates by contrasting successful and failed rollouts to isolate and edit specific local graph objects without global parameter updates.
Candidate edits are screened using a two-tier validation mechanism comprising Local Gates and Big Gates before committing changes.
Evaluated using gpt-5.6-sol, SkillAA achieved task accuracies of 81.5% on SearchQA, 66.7% on LiveMath, and 91.2% on DocVQA.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables non-parametric LLM agents to systematically diagnose, repair, and validate modular skills without global retrainings or unstructured directly-edited prompts.

papers.title: SCGFM-ART: Amortized Relational Transport for Structure-Centric Graph Foundation Models

summary.tldr: SCGFM-ART introduces Amortized Relational Transport to map heterogeneous graphs onto a shared relational atlas without costly runtime Gromov-Wasserstein optimizations, achieving fast, domain-agnostic transferability.
key_points: Relational atlas acts as a universal coordinate system using relational landmarks to decompose graphs into global response coordinates and local node-to-role correspondences.
Amortized Relational Transport (ART) directly predicts end-to-end transport plans to eliminate iterative Gromov-Wasserstein alignment at test time.
Provides mathematical proofs for coordinate fidelity bounds, stability under predicted transport plans, and an amortized coverage bound.
Achieved top average ranks on cross-domain graph-level (2.29) and node-level (1.14) classification benchmarks across 14 tasks.
Delivers 44.2x to 85.1x faster frozen target-domain inference compared to iterative alignment methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time, zero-shot transfer of graph foundation models across wildly diverse topologies and semantics by significantly speeding up target-domain inference.

papers.title: Stress-testing Alignment Midtraining

summary.tldr: An empirical stress-test of Alignment Midtraining (AMT) using models up to 110B parameters shows it fails to robustly enforce generalizable alignment motivations or unmonitored rules.
key_points: Evaluated Alignment Midtraining (AMT) at scale using models up to 110B parameters and up to 1 billion midtraining tokens.
AMT can steer model motivation in simple ambiguous post-training settings, but a tiny fraction of post-training finetuning data presenting a competing motivation completely erases AMT's effects.
Rules must be explicitly demonstrated in either midtraining or post-training datasets to be robustly learned; AMT alone does not induce generalization to unshown rules.
The authors conclude there is currently insufficient public evidence that midtraining solves the core challenges of aligning frontier AI systems.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings challenge the reliance on alignment midtraining as a reliable mechanism for out-of-distribution alignment generalization in frontier models.

papers.title: Xeno-Interpretability: Investigating the Alien Minds of LLMs

summary.tldr: This paper introduces xeno-interpretability, a framework to identify, geometrically characterize, and causally manipulate model-native internal representations that lack equivalent human concepts.
key_points: Distinguishes human-interpretable semantic space from xeno-semantic space, where internal structures lack adequate human conceptual counterparts.
Proposes separating experimental identification from semantic interpretation, allowing causal manipulation and behavioral tracking of alien representations.
Highlights safety risks in multi-agent systems where xeno-representations can propagate across interacting models while bypassing human-readable communication.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding model-native representations is critical for AI safety, as unmapped internal structures can influence LLM behavior in ways that traditional, human-concept interpretability methods miss.

papers.title: Embedding Models Measure in Peculiar Ways

summary.tldr: A study reveals that text embedding spaces fail to accurately model physical measurements of mass, distance, time, and volume, instead relying heavily on superficial string similarity.
key_points: Evaluated embedding space representations against objective physical measurements including mass, distance, time, and volume.
Discovered that physical measurement relationships are only weakly modeled within semantic embedding spaces.
Identified that embedding representations of physical measurements are strongly driven by superficial string similarity rather than actual physical scales.
Found that post-hoc recalibration of similarity metrics does not significantly improve alignment with objective physical distances.
summary.why_it_matters: Downstream applications relying on vector embeddings may make faulty reasoning errors when processing numerical or physical measurements due to the models' reliance on surface-level text features.

papers.title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers

summary.tldr: PosteriorBench is a new benchmark for evaluating the distributional accuracy and uncertainty quantification of generative inverse solvers using high-fidelity MCMC and rejection sampling reference posteriors across four physics-based problems.
key_points: Evaluates four physics-based inverse problems: Darcy flow inversion, Poisson source recovery, carbon capture and storage, and light transport material inference.
Uses computationally heavy reference posteriors generated via rejection sampling and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to evaluate full posterior distributions rather than single point estimates.
Includes a five-metric suite: posterior-mean error, posterior-standard-deviation error, maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), sliced Wasserstein distance, and radially averaged power-spectrum error.
Benchmarking reveals that neural operators enhance resolution robustness, while guidance weights and generation noise strongly influence posterior-variance calibration.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts evaluation for ill-posed inverse problems from single-reconstruction accuracy to full posterior distribution matching, helping prevent mode collapse and miscalibrated uncertainty estimates in scientific ML.

papers.title: Video DeltaNet: A Video-Native Hybrid Attention for Livestream Video Generation

summary.tldr: Video DeltaNet introduces a video-native hybrid attention mechanism combining local Softmax attention with bidirectional Video Delta Attention to enable fast, streaming video diffusion generation.
key_points: Video Delta Attention (VDA) processes long-range context by updating linear memory once per frame using its spatial tokens jointly.
Combines local Softmax attention with bidirectional linear memory using separate output projections and learnable gates, retaining Softmax for text and audio interactions.
Employs a staged teacher-alignment recipe to progressively integrate the hybrid pathway into pretrained diffusion models.
Instantiated on MiniMax H3 with eight-step distillation, completing DiT denoising for a 14.3-second 768p video in 6.70 seconds on eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs.
Achieves a 14.5x speedup over the 50-step dense H3 baseline on equivalent hardware using an optimized SGLang serving stack.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces the computational bottleneck of long spatiotemporal sequence processing in video diffusion models, enabling real-time and livestream video generation.

papers.title: An Analysis of Training-Free Self-Reported Confidence in Language Models

summary.tldr: An evaluation of three training-free confidence signals in LLMs shows direct verbalization outperforms sample agreement but remains highly sensitive to prompt phrasing and shared model misconceptions.
key_points: Direct verbalization achieves AUROC scores of 0.956 and 0.937 for correctness prediction on TriviaQA after benchmark error auditing, outperforming three-sample agreement which scored 0.765 and 0.790.
Fixed interpolation between verbalized confidence and sample agreement provides no statistically reliable performance benefit.
Self-consistency amplifies shared misconceptions, with 4 of 9 errors in one model and 2 of 8 in another receiving unanimous support across generated samples.
Re-eliciting confidence for fixed answers using equivalent prompts alters scores by 0.043 to 0.084 on average and flips 4% to 9% of correctness decisions at a 0.8 threshold.
An audit of 100 confidence-tagged biography claims reveals only a modest confidence gap between supported and contradicted claims.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on LLM self-consistency or verbalized confidence for safety-critical filtering is risky due to prompt instability and unanimous reinforcement of incorrect facts.

papers.title: Uni-LaDiR: Latent Diffusion Unifies Multimodal Reasoning

summary.tldr: Uni-LaDiR unifies multimodal reasoning by mapping multi-modal reasoning steps into a shared latent space and predicting future thought-token blocks using latent diffusion.
key_points: Uses a unified encoder to map teacher reasoning steps from diverse modalities into a single shared thought-token space.
Employs a diffusion process to generate the next block of latent thought tokens from prior context, accounting for non-deterministic reasoning paths.
Jointly trains the encoder and diffusion reasoner with shared weights to ensure thought tokens remain useful for tasks and predictable from context.
Operates at inference by generating latent thought tokens without requiring teacher observations.
Achieves relative performance improvements over strong baselines of 7.3% on visual reasoning (across 11 VLM benchmarks) and 6.1% on robot manipulation (across 2 VLA suites).
summary.why_it_matters: By eliminating the need to concatenate discrete, modality-specific thought tokens, Uni-LaDiR improves cross-modal reasoning performance in both visual language tasks and robotic control.

papers.title: Evolution or Illusion? Rethinking Evaluation in LLM Evolutionary Search

summary.tldr: A systematic evaluation protocol reveals that LLM-driven evolutionary search strategy rankings and optimal seed-versus-iteration budget allocations vary significantly across tasks and total compute budgets.
key_points: Evaluated three LLM evolutionary search strategies across five benchmark optimization tasks using a complete grid of seed counts (width) and iteration counts (depth).
Strategy rankings flip depending on compute allocation; on one task, the lowest-performing strategy at 1 seed became the top performer at 40 seeds.
Excessive iteration depth can degrade efficiency, wasting budget that yields higher performance scores if allocated to additional seeds.
Proposes a new measurement protocol that maps the explicit seeds-by-iterations Pareto frontier to evaluate search methods accurately.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-point benchmark evaluations in LLM evolutionary search yield misleading performance rankings and obscure optimal resource allocation between search width and depth.

papers.title: AutoData: Agentic Search for Pre-training Data Selection

summary.tldr: AutoData frames pre-training data selection as an agentic search over executable scoring, stratification, and stochastic algorithms using proxy model validation feedback.
key_points: Treats data selection as heuristic engineering over per-document features including lexical statistics, categorical labels, and perplexity.
Searches a rich program space of executable selection rules rather than just optimizing mixture weights over fixed domains.
Refines algorithms iteratively via execution feedback from a small proxy model within an overnight search window.
Discovered data curation recipes successfully transfer to larger training scales and improve downstream performance on the CORE benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that data pipeline engineering can be automated via LLM agents, moving data curation from manual rule design to programmatic search.

papers.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation

summary.tldr: SafeHarness improves LLM coding agents in robot manipulation by adding obstacle-aware route planning and contact execution, increasing task success to 71.9% and collision avoidance to 87.5%.
key_points: Standard LLM coding agents frequently cause collisions because their planning prioritizes task completion over safety constraints, despite perceiving obstacles correctly.
Obstacle-aware route planning grounds objects as bounding boxes, generates waypoint sequences, verifies candidates, and replans when routes become infeasible.
Obstacle-aware contact execution dynamically selects contact positions to ensure the contact action itself does not touch obstacles.
SafeHarness outperforms the prior state-of-the-art by 6.5% in task success and 27.0% in collision avoidance, representing 2.3x and 1.5x improvements over un-harnessed agents.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a method to make zero-shot LLM code-generation agents safe for real-world physical robot manipulation without requiring robot-specific model retraining.

papers.title: RAFT: A Stateful Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Troubleshooting Agents

summary.tldr: RAFT is a stateful retrieval-augmented framework that models historical troubleshooting cases as directed chains of timeline entries to perform state-matched, entry-level trajectory retrieval.
key_points: Abstracts closed historical support cases into directed chains of timeline entries and retrieves at the individual entry level rather than treating cases as static documents.
Surfaces historical cases matching the active case's intermediate state and returns the parent-case trajectory anchored at that matched state.
Optionally incorporates a case-level graph that links historical cases via configurable similarity representations.
Evaluates the standalone retrieval layer using a synthetic benchmark derived from Microsoft Learn Windows Server documentation and real human-labeled Apache Jira duplicate issues.
Outperforms vanilla RAG and GraphRAG baselines on Case Hit metrics across all stages of case progress.
summary.why_it_matters: By retrieving historical resolution trajectories based on intermediate troubleshooting states, RAFT enables customer support agents to access relevant, actionable guidance across every phase of an active case.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Falsifiers for Cyber-Physical Systems

summary.tldr: LLM-Falsifier uses large language models with iterative prompting and semantic system information to minimize Signal Temporal Logic (STL) robustness degrees and discover counterexamples in cyber-physical systems.
key_points: Converts CPS specification falsification into an LLM-driven STL robustness degree optimization problem.
Provides the LLM with semantic details like input/output names, output trajectories, and critical-time witnesses for minimum robustness.
Outperformed standard surrogate-based, Bayesian, and search-based optimization tools on 14 of 21 ARCH-COMP benchmark specifications by reducing average required simulations.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating semantic system context with LLM optimization improves sample efficiency when searching for safety-critical counterexamples in complex cyber-physical systems.

papers.title: HIL-UMI: Bringing Human-in-the-Loop Post-Training of Vision-Language-Action Models to Universal Manipulation Interface

summary.tldr: HIL-UMI is a human-in-the-loop VLA post-training framework that collects policy-guided data using a handheld Universal Manipulation Interface without requiring physical robot execution.
key_points: Uses an Energy Score to measure discrepancy between human trajectories and policy predictions on the same observation stream, triggering data collection during out-of-distribution states.
Refines a progress-based advantage estimator using low online advantage predictions to identify essential segments.
Applies advantage-conditioned behavioral cloning on a balanced dataset mixing base demonstrations and new policy data.
Outperforms HG-DAgger on the Clean Up Table task while reducing per-frame human collection time.
summary.why_it_matters: It decouples interactive, policy-aware human-in-the-loop training from physical robot hardware, enabling scalable and location-independent VLA model adaptation.

papers.title: Mitigating Retaliatory Algorithmic Collusion in Repeated Games

summary.tldr: Researchers developed CURB, a reward-shaping framework that penalizes policy total variation distance across histories to break retaliatory algorithmic collusion in general repeated games for Q-learning and deep Q-network agents.
key_points: Formalizes a connection between Q-learning collusion and Simple Penal Codes (SPCs), proving non-trivial SPCs induce conditional policy dependence measurable via total variation (TV) distance across cooperation and defection histories.
Introduces CURB (Collusion Unwinding via Reward shaping and Belief injection), which penalizes this TV distance signal during Q-learning.
Guarantees the conversion of any SPC fixed point of the learning dynamics into a trivial one, eliminating collusive equilibria driven by punishment threats.
Demonstrates empirical collusion reduction in tabular Q-learning across Bertrand and Cournot competition repeated games, as well as Deep Q-Network (DQN) agents in Bertrand competition.
summary.why_it_matters: CURB offers a general, theoretical framework to prevent autonomous reinforcement learning agents from establishing tacit, retaliatory collusive pricing without requiring domain-specific interventions.

papers.title: Language-model groups overstate consensus when replaying human deliberation on a reasoning task

summary.tldr: LLM agent groups replaying human deliberative reasoning overstate full-consensus rates by 34 to 44 percentage points compared to humans, often agreeing unanimously on incorrect answers.
key_points: Replayed 100 held-out human Wason selection task groups with belief-anchored LLM agent groups using both chat and reasoning modes.
Human consensus estimates varied from 24.0% to 57.0% depending on operationalization, partly because nearly one-fifth of human participants never posted, whereas agents almost always participated.

Post-unblinding sensitivity analyses (submit-based n=98, participation-matched n=45) converged within 0.5 percentage points, showing consensus gaps of 34.0–34.1 points for chat mode and 43.9–44.4 points for reasoning mode.
Removing early stopping and reparameterizing to eliminate memorizable answers caused reasoning-mode agent groups to achieve near-unanimous consensus, primarily on incorrect answers.
summary.why_it_matters: Simulated multi-agent LLM consensus does not reliably reflect collective accuracy or human deliberative group-outcome distributions on reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Refuse, Decompose, Refresh: A Claim-Safe Protocol for Closed-Loop AI Evaluation

summary.tldr: A claim-safe closed-loop AI evaluation protocol uses three core actions—Refuse, Decompose, and Refresh—to prevent invalid claims caused by policy-driven state changes and distribution shifts.
key_points: The protocol enforces three actions: Refuse (abstain when reference stream lacks support), Decompose (report execution, false admission, and structural hypotheses separately), and Refresh (recompute reference maps during drift alarms).
In a 1,440-case heldout evaluation with 72 regime-component units, the protocol refused 17 non-admitted units, achieving a 0/20 stable false admission rate with a 95% upper bound of 0.1391.
Within admitted units, affected clean traffic outpredicted nominal fault-cell fraction by a negative-log-likelihood difference of 0.1264 nats per row across 540 unit-arm rows.
Clean fault-null streams triggered distribution-shift alarms in 15/15, 0/15, and 14/15 cases across three demand regimes, proving null states depend directly on detector reference alignment.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents false conclusions in closed-loop AI evaluations by ensuring pass/fail claims are mathematically supported and properly calibrated against runtime state shifts.

papers.title: The Organization of Inference: Information, Resource Constraints, and AI Production

summary.tldr: Controlled experiments on software-engineering tasks reveal that organizational workflows and task-information access dictate whether increased token capacity translates into higher inference success rates.
key_points: Direct execution achieved a constant 59.6% success rate across 12,000 and 24,000 logical-token ceilings, whereas information-constrained planning rose from 36.2% to 51.2% success.
Providing issue access to a read-only planner at a 12,000-token ceiling increased success by ~16 percentage points over issue-hidden planning.
Task-informed planning lagged direct execution by ~10 points at 12,000 tokens but outperformed it by 29.6 percentage points at 24,000 tokens.
Increasing token limits dropped the planning workflow's binding rate from 46.2% to 0.8%, with downstream execution driving 89.9% of the total token use increase.
summary.why_it_matters: Scaling inference compute yields minimal performance gains unless the underlying agent workflow and information structure are optimized to utilize the extra capacity.

papers.title: Accelerating Sharded Data Parallelism at Scale with Federated Learning

summary.tldr: FL+FSDP and FL+HSDP hybrid algorithms combine sharded data parallelism with FedAvg-style aggregations to reduce multi-tier interconnect overhead during large-scale foundation model pre-training.
key_points: Decouples large data parallel deployments into smaller, loosely-coupled federation groups to minimize inter-group traffic.
Bounds the global batch size growth relative to the size of the federation groups rather than total GPU count.
Achieves up to 8.04x faster data processing and 4.48 points lower evaluation perplexity over standard FSDP and HSDP when pre-training Llama 3.1 8B on 512 A100 GPUs.
summary.why_it_matters: The approach significantly reduces communication bottlenecks on heterogeneous multi-tier GPU clusters, improving both training throughput and final model quality for large foundation models.

papers.title: QUALS: Corpus Equilibrium for Universal Forecasting via Pattern Quantization and Learnability Synchronization

summary.tldr: QUALS is a time series corpus equilibrium framework that uses pattern quantization and learnability synchronization to dramatically improve foundation model zero-shot forecasting efficiency on reduced training data.
key_points: Addresses inefficient data sampling and distribution management in foundation model pre-training across diverse domain datasets.
Employs a pattern quantization framework that decodes heterogeneous temporal patterns using vector quantization and uniform binning.
Uses a learnability synchronization framework to calibrate sampling weights across heterogeneous patterns, reducing the optimization gap between simple and complex motifs.
Achieves superior zero-shot forecasting performance while using only a small fraction of the original pre-training budget.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables foundation models for time series forecasting to achieve higher zero-shot accuracy while drastically lowering the computational costs and data volume required for pre-training.

security.title: s-MDM: Generative Virtualization of Multi-Device Hardware Variations for Portable DL-SCA

summary.tldr: s-MDM is a zero-target-trace generative framework that uses a cVAE with continuous style modulation to synthesize virtual multi-device side-channel profiles, improving deep learning portability across hardware variations.
key_points: Combines a structured cVAE generator, a Walsh-Hadamard leakage anchor, continuous style modulation, and decoupled leakage-style--domain critics.
Operates offline without requiring traces from the target device.
Evaluated on 32-bit AES_PTv2 side-channel traces to address layout shifts, silicon process variations, and noise shifts.
Outperforms physical baselines in maintaining a low key rank on layout- and acquisition-shifted targets like the Pinata target, though physical MDM remains superior on identical hardware clones (D4).
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deep learning side-channel attacks to generalize to unseen target hardware without needing physical access to target traces beforehand.

security.title: Unmasking Cloud Identities: From Behavioral Clustering to Automated Detection

summary.tldr: Unit 42 designed a behavioral clustering model that maps cloud identity roles from audit logs to enable continuous threat detection via SQL queries.
key_points: Maps cloud identity roles directly from cloud audit logs using a behavioral clustering model.
Enables continuous threat detection capabilities executed through standard SQL queries.
summary.why_it_matters: Security teams can automate cloud identity role mapping and perform continuous threat detection directly using standard database queries.
